title: Denorm and dynamic scaling strategy draft for inference runtime
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working draft exploring a set of mitigations for observed NaNs and extreme instability in FP16 inference runs at long context lengths and high batching concurrency. The focus is on: denormal (subnormal) value handling, dynamic multiplicative scaling (per-layer/per-head), accumulation strategy (FP16 vs FP32 accumulators), and how KV cache re-use + scheduler batching can interact to surface numerical breakages.

Background / problem statement:
- We see sporadic NaNs in attention outputs when serving certain open models (Llama-family variants) in FP16 builds under realistic production workloads. Failures are correlated with: long context (>= 1024), mixed batch sizes, and sessions that reuse KV cache across requests with different token distributions.
- Root cause hypothesis (working): a combination of extremely small values (denormals) during softmax / attention that get flush-to-zero/handled inconsistently across kernels, plus repeated scaling/quantization of KV cache during background requantization paths causes exponent drift. When small mantissas are multiplied repeatedly in accumulator-limited precision, underflow or catastrophic cancellation can cause NaNs when downstream ops apply divides or exponentials.
- Observations from recent runs (log snippets in PR #479):
  - NaNs appear first in attention logits for specific heads, then propagate to output tokens after layernorms.
  - Turning on "flush-to-zero" at the kernel-level prevents some cases but hides diagnostics and occasionally degrades generation quality (tiny probability mass lost).
  - Long-lived KV cache entries that were requantized between FP32->FP16 (for disk/network) and then used back-to-back with unscaled live outputs produce mismatched exponent ranges.

Design goals and constraints:
- Minimize latency regression (<= 5% P50 change target) and memory impact.
- Maintain generation quality; avoid blind F2Z if it measurably changes token probabilities in evals.
- Provide robust fallback that keeps serving live rather than returning errors when numerical instability is detected.
- Make changes incremental and observable; prefer knobs we can flag remotely and A/B via rollouts.

Proposed mitigation strategies (shortlist):
1) Promote accumulation to FP32 in critical kernels (attention matmul accumulators)
   - Implement local accumulation in FP32 for matmul-based attention (A * B^T) but keep inputs/outputs in FP16.
   - Cost: modest extra compute and memory for tile accumulators; expected to recover stability in most cases.
2) Dynamic multiplicative scaling with max-abs tracking (exponent tracking)
   - Track a running max-abs per-layer (or per-head) during the first N tokens of a request and compute a scale s = 2^{k} to bring values into a safer exponent band. Apply the inverse scale after the critical ops.
   - Provide a small metadata header in KV cache (scale exponent) so cached K/V blocks carry their scaling provenance. Reuse path must rescale cached blocks to current request scale before accumulation.
3) Conditional denorm-to-zero or denorm-to-fp32 path for certain ops
   - If a kernel detects a high fraction (> threshold) of subnormal exponents in a tile, route that tile through a FP32 slow path or perform a local normalization step to avoid repeated underflow.
4) KV cache metadata and requantization policy
   - Extend KV cache format to include: scale_exponent, dtype_hint, checksum. When fetching cached blocks, runtime compares scale_exponent with the current request's expected exponent; if the delta > limit, schedule on-the-fly requantization or promote temporarily to FP32 accumulators.
   - This avoids silent mixing of different exponent bands which we think amplifies cancellation.
5) Observability and automatic fallback rules
   - Expose per-request metrics: fraction_denorms, max_abs_per_layer, exponent_histogram, NaN_count-in-flight.
   - If NaN_count or abrupt exponent spikes observed, route request to a higher-precision variant (model-xx-fp32 or model-xx-bf16) transparently with automatic rollback.
6) Avoid global flush-to-zero as default; prefer localized handling with feature flags.

Kernel / implementation notes (low level):
- Attention kernel changes: promote inner reduction accumulator to float32; keep block GEMM inputs still FP16, compute products in FP16->promote->accumulate in FP32, cast out to FP16 at end (with optional requant/rescale). Reuse existing vectorized FP32 accumulators where available.
- Softmax numerics: compute softmax in FP32 if input dynamic range exceeds threshold; otherwise use stabilized FP16 softmax with per-row max subtraction. Consider multi-lane reduction to compute max_abs cheaply.
- Per-tile dynamic normalization: implement a fast pass that computes tile max-abs using a fused intra-warp reduction (cheap) and stores exponent k. If k outside [-16, +16], apply local shift to bring tile to target exponent band.
- KV cache storage: add a 16-bit header per block: (scale_exponent:int8, dtype:uint8, flags:uint8). Keep backward compatibility by inferring if header missing (legacy caches treated as scale_exponent=0).

Scheduler interactions and edge cases:
- Mixed batch scheduler currently merges requests into batches without checking per-request scale metadata; update scheduler to partition batches by scale_exponent when the delta would cause differing accumulation paths. This slightly reduces batching efficiency but prevents mixing incompatible blocks.
- Implement a batch coalescing heuristic: allow mixing when delta <= 2 exponents; otherwise split into separate kernel launches.
- KV cache re-use across sessions: when serving identical sessions across different hardware (some with F2Z on, some with strict IEEE), ensure cache entries advertise hardware feature flags; router should avoid serving cached entries from incompatible nodes unless re-quantized.

Experiments to run (short-term):
1) Canary: enable FP32 accumulators for attention matmul on a small Dedicated pool (20% of requests) for 48h. Collect NaN_count, latency P50/P95, token-level generation divergence vs control.
2) Simulate worst-case requant churn: produce synthetic workload that alternates requantization of KV cache and live stream writes; validate exponent mismatches and verification checksum.
3) Evaluate scale metadata approach: add header to newly created KV caches in dev environment and exercise mixed-scale batch joins; measure batch split frequency and latency impact.
4) Softmax FP32 fallback: instrument thresholding and run on 500 validation prompts to measure change in predicted next-token probabilities.

Failure modes and open questions:
- Cost/latency tradeoff: promoting accumulators to FP32 will increase DRAM traffic for accumulators; need microbenchmarks to quantify P50/P95 changes on target hardware (A100/H100/GPU types).
- Interaction with quantization pipelines (4-bit aware quant, QAT) — how does dynamic scaling align with learned scale params? Could produce bias if not applied symmetrically.
- Correctness vs determinism: per-request dynamic scaling may produce run-to-run variability. We need to decide acceptable variance for production (likely small but not zero).
- How to roll out KV-cache header without breaking long-lived caches persisted in object store; plan is fallback-to-legacy interpretation and gradual migration.

Action items and owners:
- (Priya) Prototype FP32 accumulator path in matmul kernel (dev branch: fp32-accum-proto). Due: 2025-02-10.
- (Marco) Add KV cache header prototype and metadata plumbing for scale_exponent. Due: 2025-02-17.
- (Evelyn) Implement lightweight per-tile max-abs reducer and metrics; add telemetry for fraction_denorms. Due: 2025-02-12.
- (Jonah) Design scheduler batching heuristic and simulate split cost. Due: 2025-02-20.
- (Team) Run canary with combined mitigations and collect 72h metrics; decision gate for wider rollout after analysis. Gate review: 2025-03-03.

Test harness / reproduction steps (dev instructions):
- Repro script: tools/repro/denorm_repro.py --model model-llama-13b-fp16 --ctx 2048 --batch-pattern "[1,8,4,1,16]" --requant-cycle 10 --duration 600
- Canary test: infra canary config: infra/canaries/denorm-fp32-accum.yaml (20% traffic).
- Metric dashboard: observability/query?panel=denorms (dashboard prototype in PR #479).

Notes to reviewers / discussion points:
- Are we comfortable with adding scale metadata to KV cache vs doing only runtime promotion? Scale metadata gives us much finer control for reuse but increases cache size / complexity.
- Should we prefer bf16 as a default alternative to fp16 on newer hardware? bf16 preserves exponent range at the same width; however not all GPUs/nodes have bf16 fast-paths.
- If we go with FP32 accumulators, consider adding an opt-in compilation path that turns this on only for specific model families known to be sensitive.

Appendix: brief experiment logs (copied from kernel CI runs)
- 2024-12-22: run A (A100), 10k requests synthetic; NaN_count=42; enabling FP32 accumulators reduced NaN_count to 0 in same workload but increased mean latency by 3.6%.
- 2024-12-30: run B (mixed batch), observed exponent histogram spikes in head 7, layers 10-12; fraction_denorms peaked at 11%.

This document is intentionally a working draft — please add inline comments, link additional failure examples, and push small patches with the branch naming convention: denorm-<owner>-<short-tag>.
